readings.title: Woe to Drunken Ephrayim
readings.subtitle: A Crown of Splendour for the Remnant
readings.text: [Isaiah 28:1] Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephrayim, and to the fading flower of its splendid comeliness that is on the head of the fertile valley, to those who are overcome with wine! [2] See, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has one who is strong and potent, like a downpour of hail and a destroying storm, like a flood of mighty waters overflowing, who casts down to the earth with the hand. [3] The proud crown of the drunkards of Ephrayim, is trampled under foot; [4] and the fading flower of its splendid comeliness that is on the head of the fertile valley, like the first fruit before the summer, which, when one sees it, he eats it up while it is still in his hand. [5] In that day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is for a crown of splendour and a head-dress of comeliness to the remnant of <dn>His</dn> people, [6] and a spirit of right-ruling to him who sits in right-ruling, and strength to those who turn back the battle at the gate.

readings.title: Astray Through Strong Drink
readings.subtitle: Command Upon Command, Line Upon Line
readings.text: [Isaiah 28:7] And these too have gone astray through wine, and through strong drink wandered about. Priest and prophet have gone astray through strong drink, they are swallowed up by wine, they wander about through strong drink, they go astray in vision, they stumble in right-ruling. [8] For all tables shall be covered with vomit, no place without filth. [9] Whom would <dn>He</dn> teach <dn>את</dn> knowledge? And whom would <dn>He</dn> make to understand <dn>את</dn> the message? Those weaned from milk, those taken from the breasts! [10] For it is: command upon command, command upon command, line upon line, line upon line, here a little, there a little. [11] For with a jabbering lip and a foreign tongue <dn>He</dn> speaks to this people, [12] to whom <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“This is the rest, give rest to the weary,”</dq> and, <dq>“This is the refreshing.”</dq> But they would not hear. [13] But the Word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was to them, “Command upon command, command upon command, line upon line, line upon line, here a little, there a little,” so that they go and shall stumble backward, and be broken and snared and taken captive.

readings.title: A Covenant with Death
readings.subtitle: The Precious Cornerstone in Tsiyon
readings.text: [Isaiah 28:14] Therefore hear <dn>את</dn> the Word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, you men of scorn, who rule this people who are in Yerushalayim, [15] because you have said, “We have made a covenant with death, and with She’ol we have effected a vision. When the overflowing scourge passes through, it does not come to us, for we have made lying our refuge, and under falsehood we have hidden ourselves.” [16] Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am laying in Tsiyon a stone for a foundation, a tried stone, a precious corner-stone, a settled foundation. He who trusts shall not hasten away.</dq> [17] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall make right-ruling the measuring line, and righteousness the plummet. And the hail shall sweep away <dn>את</dn> the refuge of lying, and the waters overflow <dn>את</dn> the hiding place.</dq> [18] <dq>And your covenant with death shall be annulled, and your vision with She’ol not stand. When an overflowing scourge passes through, then you shall be trampled down by it.</dq> [19] <dq>As often as it passes through it shall take you, for it shall pass through every morning, and by day and by night. And it shall be only trembling to understand the message.”</dq> [20] For the bed shall be too short for a man to stretch out on, and the covering shall be too narrow to wrap himself in it. [21] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rises up as at Mount Peratsim, and <dn>He</dn> is wroth as at the Valley of Giḇ‛on, to do <dn>His</dn> work, <dn>His</dn> strange work, and to do <dn>His</dn> deed, <dn>His</dn> strange deed. [22] And now, do not be scoffers, lest your bonds be made strong. For <dn>I</dn> have heard from the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, a destruction decreed upon all the earth.

readings.title: The Parable of the Farmer
readings.subtitle: The Wonderful Counsel of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Isaiah 28:23] Give ear and hear <dn>My</dn> voice, listen and hear <dn>My</dn> Word. [24] Does the ploughman keep ploughing all day to sow? Does he keep turning his soil and breaking the clods? [25] When he has levelled its surface, does he not sow the caraway and scatter the cummin, plant the wheat in rows, the barley in the appointed place, and the spelt in its place? [26] For <dn>He</dn> instructs him for right-ruling, his <dn>Elohim</dn> teaches him. [27] For caraway is not threshed with a threshing sledge, nor is a wagon wheel rolled over cummin, but caraway is beaten out with a stick, and cummin with a rod. [28] Grain is crushed, so one does not go on threshing it forever, nor break it with his wagon wheel, nor crush it with his horsemen. [29] Even this has come from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, who did wonders in counsel, who made wisdom great.

readings.title: The Siege of Shomeron
readings.subtitle: Assyria Besieges the Capital for Three Years
readings.text: [2 Kings 17:5] And the sovereign of Ashshur went through all the land, and went up to Shomeron and besieged <dn>את</dn> it for three years.

readings.title: The Fall of Shomeron
readings.subtitle: Israel Exiled for Disobedience
readings.text: [2 Kings 18:9] And it came to be in the fourth year of Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu, which was the seventh year of Hoshěa son of Ělah, sovereign of Yisra’ěl, that Shalmaneser sovereign of Ashshur came up against Shomeron and besieged it, [10] and they captured <dn>את</dn> it at the end of three years. In the sixth year of Ḥizqiyah, that is the ninth year of Hoshěa sovereign of Yisra’ěl, Shomeron was captured. [11] And the sovereign of Ashshur exiled <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl to Ashshur, and placed them in Ḥalaḥ and Ḥaḇor, the River of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes, [12] because they did not obey <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, but transgressed <dn>His</dn> covenant – all that Mosheh the servant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded. And they did not obey nor do them.

readings.title: Why Israel Was Exiled
readings.subtitle: A Litany of Idolatry and Rebellion
readings.text: [2 Kings 17:6] In the ninth year of Hoshěa, the sovereign of Ashshur captured <dn>את</dn> Shomeron and exiled <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl to Ashshur, and settled them in Ḥalaḥ and Ḥaḇor, the River of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes. [7] Now this came to be because the children of Yisra’ěl had sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn> – who had brought them up out of the land of Mitsrayim, from under the hand of Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim – and feared <dn>את</dn> other mighty ones, [8] and walked in the laws of the nations whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had dispossessed from before the children of Yisra’ěl, and of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl that they had made. [9] And the children of Yisra’ěl secretly did against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn> matters that were not right, and they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from watchtower unto the walled city, [10] and set up for themselves pillars and Ashěrim on every high hill and under every green tree, [11] and burned incense there on all the high places, like the nations whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had removed from their presence. And they did <dn>את</dn> evil matters to provoke <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [12] and served <dn>את</dn> the idols, of which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said to them, <dq>“Do not do this.”</dq> [13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> warned <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl and <dn>את</dn> Yehuḏah, through all of <dn>His</dn> prophets, and every seer, saying, <dq>“Turn back from your evil ways, and guard <dn>My</dn> commands and <dn>My</dn> laws, according to all the Torah which <dn>I</dn> commanded your fathers, and which <dn>I</dn> sent to you by <dn>My</dn> servants the prophets.”</dq> [14] But they did not listen and hardened their necks, like the necks of their fathers, who did not put their trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, [15] and rejected <dn>His</dn> laws and <dn>His</dn> covenant that <dn>He</dn> had made with their fathers, and <dn>His</dn> witnesses which <dn>He</dn> had witnessed against them, and went after worthlessness, and became worthless, and after the nations who were all around them, of whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded them not to do like them. [16] And they left all the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, and made for themselves a moulded image, two calves, and made an Ashěrah and bowed themselves to all the host of the heavens, and served <dn>את</dn> Ba‛al, [17] and caused their sons and daughters to pass through the fire, and practised divination and sorcery, and sold themselves to do <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to provoke <dn>Him</dn>. [18] So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was very enraged with Yisra’ěl, and removed them from <dn>His</dn> presence – none was left but the tribe of Yehuḏah alone.

readings.title: Judah's Sin and Israel's Final Removal
readings.subtitle: Cast Out from the Presence of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [2 Kings 17:19] Yehuḏah, also, did not guard <dn>את</dn> the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, but walked in the laws of Yisra’ěl which they made. [20] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rejected <dn>את</dn> all the seed of Yisra’ěl, and afflicted them, and gave them into the hand of plunderers, until <dn>He</dn> had cast them out from <dn>His</dn> presence. [21] For <dn>He</dn> tore <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from the house of Daviḏ, and they made Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat sovereign. And Yaroḇ‛am drove <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and made them commit a great sin. [22] And the children of Yisra’ěl walked in all the sins of Yaroḇ‛am which he did. They did not turn away from them, [23] until <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> removed <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from <dn>His</dn> presence, as <dn>He</dn> spoke by all <dn>His</dn> servants the prophets. So Yisra’ěl was exiled from their land to Ashshur, as it is to this day.

readings.title: The Resettlement of Shomeron
readings.subtitle: Lions and a Syncretistic Religion
readings.text: [2 Kings 17:24] And the sovereign of Ashshur brought people from Baḇel, and from Kuthah, and from Avva, and from Ḥamath, and Sepharvayim, and placed them in the cities of Shomeron instead of the children of Yisra’ěl. And they took possession of Shomeron and dwelt in its cities. [25] And it came to be, at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they did not fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent <dn>את</dn> lions among them, which were killing among them. [26] And they spoke to the sovereign of Ashshur, saying, “The nations whom you have removed and placed in the cities of Shomeron do not know <dn>את</dn> the right-ruling of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of the land. And <dn>He</dn> has sent <dn>את</dn> lions among them, and see, they are slaying among them because they do not know <dn>את</dn> the right-ruling of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of the land.” [27] And the sovereign of Ashshur commanded, saying, “Send one of the priests whom you exiled from there, to go there. Let him go and dwell there, and let him teach them <dn>את</dn> the right-ruling of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of the land.” [28] And one of the priests whom they had exiled from Shomeron came and dwelt in Běyth Ěl, and taught them how to fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [29] But every nation was making mighty ones of its own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Shomeronim had made, every nation in the cities where they dwelt. [30] And the men of Baḇel made Sukkoth Benoth, and the men of Kuth made Něrḡal, and the men of Ḥamath made Ashima, [31] and the Avvites made Niḇḥaz and Tartaq. And the Sepharvites burned their children in fire to Aḏrammeleḵ and Anammeleḵ, the mighty ones of Sepharim. [32] They also feared <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and from every class they made for themselves priests of the high places, who offered for them in the house of the high places. [33] They were fearing <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and they were serving <dn>את</dn> their own mighty ones, according to the ruling of the nations from among whom they had been exiled.

readings.title: A People of Divided Loyalties
readings.subtitle: Fearing YeHoVaH While Serving Idols
readings.text: [2 Kings 17:34] To this day they are doing according to the former rulings: they are not fearing <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor do they follow their laws or their right-rulings, or the Torah and command which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> the children of Ya‛aqoḇ, whose name <dn>He</dn> made Yisra’ěl, [35] with whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had made a covenant and commanded them, saying, <dq>“Do not fear <dn>את</dn> other mighty ones, nor bow down to them nor serve them nor slaughter to them;</dq> [36] <dq>but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who brought you up from the land of Mitsrayim with great power and with an outstretched arm, <dn>את</dn> <dn>Him</dn> you shall fear, and to <dn>Him</dn> you shall bow yourselves, and to <dn>Him</dn> you shall slaughter.</dq> [37] <dq>And guard to do forever <dn>את</dn> the laws, and <dn>את</dn> the right-rulings, and <dn>את</dn> the Torah, and <dn>את</dn> the command which <dn>He</dn> wrote for you. And do not fear <dn>את</dn> other mighty ones.</dq> [38] <dq>And do not forget <dn>את</dn> the covenant that <dn>I</dn> have made with you, and do not fear <dn>את</dn> other mighty ones.</dq> [39] <dq>But fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, so that <dn>He</dn> delivers you from the hand of all your enemies.”</dq> [40] And they did not obey, but did according to their former ruling. [41] So these nations were fearing <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and served their carved images, both their children and their children’s children. As their fathers did, they are doing to this day.

readings.title: The Vision of Yeshayahu
readings.subtitle: A Rebellious and Wounded Nation
readings.text: [Isaiah 1:1] The vision of Yeshayahu son of Amots, which he saw concerning Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim in the days of Uzziyahu, Yotham, Aḥaz, Ḥizqiyahu – sovereigns of Yehuḏah. [2] Hear, O heavens, and listen, O earth! For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have reared and brought up children, but they have transgressed against <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>An ox knows <dn>את</dn> its owner and a donkey <dn>את</dn> its master’s crib – Yisra’ěl does not know, <dn>My</dn> people have not understood.”</dq> [4] Alas, sinning nation, a people loaded with crookedness, a seed of evil-doers, sons acting corruptly! They have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, they have provoked <dn>את</dn> the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl, they went backward. [5] Why should you be stricken any more? You continue in apostasy! All the head is sick, and all the heart faints. [6] From the sole of the foot, to the head, there is no soundness in it – wounds and bruises and open sores; they have not been closed or bound up, or soothed with ointment. [7] Your land is laid waste, your cities are burned with fire, strangers devour your land in your presence. And it is laid waste, as overthrown by strangers. [8] And the daughter of Tsiyon is left as a booth in a vineyard, as a hut in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city. [9] Unless <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts had left to us a small remnant, we would have become like Seḏom, we would have been made like Amorah.

readings.title: A Call to Repentance
readings.subtitle: Though Your Sins Are Like Scarlet
readings.text: [Isaiah 1:10] Hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, you rulers of Seḏom; give ear to the Torah of our <dn>Elohim</dn>, you people of Amorah! [11] <dq>“Of what use to <dn>Me</dn> are your many slaughterings?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have had enough of ascending offerings of rams and the fat of fed beasts. <dn>I</dn> do not delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs or goats.</dq> [12] <dq>When you come to appear before <dn>Me</dn>, who has required this from your hand, to trample <dn>My</dn> courtyards?</dq> [13] <dq>Stop bringing futile offerings, incense, it is an abomination to <dn>Me</dn>. New moons, Sabbaths, the calling of gatherings – <dn>I</dn> am unable to bear unrighteousness and assembly.</dq> [14] <dq><dn>My</dn> being hates your New moons and your appointed times, they are a trouble to <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> am weary of bearing them.</dq> [15] <dq>And when you spread out your hands, <dn>I</dn> hide <dn>My</dn> eyes from you; even though you make many prayers, <dn>I</dn> do not hear. Your hands have become filled with blood.</dq> [16] <dq>Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; put away <dn>את</dn> the evil of your doings from before <dn>My</dn> eyes. Stop doing evil!</dq> [17] <dq>Learn to do good! Seek right-ruling, reprove the oppressor, defend the fatherless, plead for the widow.</dq> [18] <dq>Come now, and let us reason together,”</dq> says <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall be as wool.</dq> [19] <dq>If you submit and obey, you shall eat <dn>את</dn> the good of the land;</dq> [20] <dq>but if you refuse and rebel, you shall be devoured by the sword,”</dq> for the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken.
